title: Payment Operations Standard — Grace Start for a Pre-Suspension Installment on Payment Arrangements
content:
How an installment's debit came back decides where its pre-suspension grace starts, for a suspended plan under Payment Arrangements.

## Standard

The grace start follows how the examined installment's debit came back:

- when its most recent return was for account closed or stop payment, the debit is never presented again and the grace starts on the date that return was received;
- when it was for NSF, unauthorized debit or card chargeback, the grace starts on the date its debit was last presented;
- when it was never returned, the grace starts on its scheduled due date.

The returns and presentments are read from the plan's installment history for that installment only: its returned installment payment entries (the latest one by date received gives the most recent return and its reason) and its installment payment entries (the latest one by date gives the date the debit was last presented).

## Table

| Most recent return of the examined installment | Grace starts on |
|---|---|
| Account closed | The date that return was received |
| Stop payment | The date that return was received |
| NSF | The date the debit was last presented |
| Unauthorized debit | The date the debit was last presented |
| Card chargeback | The date the debit was last presented |
| Never returned | The installment's scheduled due date |

## Hypothetical installment histories

- Installment due 5 April, debited 5 April, returned for NSF on 8 April, presented again on 12 April and returned for NSF on 15 April: the most recent return is NSF and the debit was last presented on 12 April — the grace starts on 12 April.
- Installment due 5 April, debited 5 April, returned for stop payment on 9 April: the grace starts on 9 April.
- Installment due 5 April, debited and never returned: the grace starts on 5 April.
